back: The Shona title of a king; the Rozvi rulers were called Mambo.
Worship of the high god Mwari through shrines, notably in the Matobo Hills, whose priests were consulted for rain and guidance.

front: Which was the capital of the Torwa state?

back: Changamire Dombo, in the late seventeenth century.

front: Which Nguni leaders attacked the Rozvi in the 1830s?
back: Zwangendaba and Nxaba; then Mzilikazi's Ndebele settled the south-west about 1838-40.

front: How did the Rozvi gain control of the plateau?
back: Changamire Dombo built a strong army, overthrew the Torwa, defeated the Mutapa and drove the Portuguese from the plateau.

front: Why did the Rozvi state decline?
back: Succession disputes and independent provinces weakened it, then Nguni invasions in the 1830s and the Ndebele finished it.

front: How did the Mwari cult support the Rozvi?
back: Its priests spoke for the high god on rain and harvest, giving the rulers divine support and uniting many peoples.
